subject.title: Feature: configurable mediaLocalRoots for image tool

question: Which canonical operator-controlled host-root policy should OpenClaw support for image/media tools: shared tools.fs.roots, a narrower media-only root field, or no persistent host-root expansion?
rationale: The request changes what model-facing media tools may read from the host, and repository policy treats filesystem boundaries plus config/default surfaces as security-sensitive product decisions rather than safe autonomous fixes.

options.title: Use shared filesystem roots
options.body: Adopt a single security-reviewed tools.fs.roots-style contract for filesystem tools and media paths so OpenClaw does not grow competing allowlists.

options.title: Add media-only roots
options.body: Add a narrower media-root config only if maintainers want image/PDF/media reads decoupled from read/write/edit filesystem policy, with explicit docs and split-boundary tests.

options.title: Keep current boundary
options.body: Continue requiring managed inbound media, scoped channel attachment roots, copies, or symlinks instead of persistent host-root expansion.

recommendation.title: Use shared filesystem roots
recommendation.body: Adopt a single security-reviewed tools.fs.roots-style contract for filesystem tools and media paths so OpenClaw does not grow competing allowlists.

likelyOwner.reason: The strongest current history on the media-root resolver, filesystem policy gating, and config schema points to steipete as the best available owner for the security/product contract choice.
